lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the woody twining yellow-flowered Gelsemium branch and its capsule/winged-seed architecture as a modern family split from Loganiaceae.

project_scope.note: Single project taxon. Older literature often placed Gelsemium in Loganiaceae; current FNA/Kew classification recognizes Gelsemiaceae.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for a woody twining vine with opposite simple leaves and fragrant yellow tubular/funnelform flowers. Confirm with an elliptic/oblong septicidal capsule that splits into four segments and seeds with a unilateral wing.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Woody climbers/vines or shrubs. Leaves opposite, simple, entire and exstipulate in the ordinary sense, but small stipular colleters occur near petiole bases in Gelsemium.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers solitary or in small cymes, 5-merous with a fused yellow to orange corolla. Gelsemium can be heterostylous, with pin and thrum flowers differing in style/stamen position.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Elliptic to oblong septicidal capsule, splitting into four segments. Gelsemium sempervirens seeds are unilaterally winged.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Yellow twining jessamine + opposite leaves + dry 4-segment capsule with winged seeds = Gelsemiaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: twining vine → yellow fused flower → pin/thrum clue → 4-segment capsule → winged seed → old Loganiaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Gelsemiaceae is a small family in our pool but an excellent lineage lesson: an old Loganiaceae member that becomes easy to remember once the winged seed is seen.

steps.title: 1 · Recognize the woody twining habit
steps.look_for: Evergreen/semi-evergreen twining stems with opposite glossy/simple leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: This instantly separates it from the small herbaceous Gentianaceae and local Loganiaceae anchors.

steps.title: 2 · Find the yellow fused flower
steps.look_for: Fragrant yellow funnelform/tubular corolla, usually solitary or in very small cymes.
steps.why_it_matters: The flower explains the common 'jessamine' look while retaining the Gentianales fused-corolla pattern.

steps.title: 3 · Learn pin vs thrum
steps.look_for: Some flowers have long styles/short stamens and others short styles/long stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: Heterostyly is a memorable reproductive detail in Gelsemium sempervirens.

steps.title: 4 · Open the dry capsule
steps.look_for: An elliptic/oblong capsule opening septicidally into four segments.
steps.why_it_matters: This separates the vine from berry-fruited lookalikes.

steps.title: 5 · Find the unilateral seed wing
steps.look_for: Flat seed with a conspicuous wing extending mainly from one side.
steps.why_it_matters: This is an excellent confirmation character for G. sempervirens.

comparisons.title: Gelsemiaceae vs Loganiaceae
comparisons.rule: Older sources may place Gelsemium in Loganiaceae. Current learner separates it: woody twining Gelsemium with yellow flowers and winged seeds versus local herbaceous Spigelia/Mitreola and their different capsule architecture.

comparisons.title: Gelsemiaceae vs Apocynaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can be opposite-leaved woody vines with fused flowers. Gelsemium lacks the classic milky-latex clue and produces a septicidal 4-segment capsule with winged seeds rather than the common paired-follicle Apocynaceae pattern.

comparisons.title: Gelsemiaceae vs Gentianaceae
comparisons.rule: Gelsemium is woody/twining and has winged seeds; local gentians are herbs with many-seeded capsules and no ordinary stipules.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use yellow flowers alone—many unrelated vines flower yellow. Confirm habit, opposite leaves, capsule and seed.

genera.fast_cue: twining woody vine + opposite leaves + yellow fused flowers + 4-segment capsule + winged seeds
